newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo gold futures rise on firmer bullion prices.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo gold futures rise on firmer bullion prices.

text.p: Yen-based Tokyo gold futures ended firmer across the board on Friday, supported by firmer bullion prices and the yen's weaker tendency against the dollar, traders said.
Gold futures ranged from seven to 15 yen per gram firmer, with benchmark October finishing up 13 yen at 1,323 yen.
In the bullion market, spot gold was quoted at $358.30/80 per ounce at 0731 GMT, against $357.80/358.20 in New York on Thursday.
"Spot gold market has firmed, buoyed by fund short-covering during Asian hours," one trader said.

In the gold futures market, two-way business was detected. After opening firmer, gold futures were stuck in tight ranges in the afternoon session as the yen's rebound later in the day was offset by firmer bullion prices.

Despite the short-covering-led rallies in the bullion market, bearish sentiment remained intact as physical buyers in Asia were sidelined as they were not convinced that prices have hit bottom, traders said.
"Asian buyers are expected to step into the market before spot gold breaks under $350 per ounce," an senior official of a bullion house said.
Focus is on the announcement of U.S. employment date due later today to see any impact on U.S. financial markets.
Platinum futures settled firmer on the heels of gold, while palladium futures cut early gains to end barely firmer, pressured by profit-taking.

Although the plunge in stock prices has failed so far to have an immediate impact on the precious metals market, investors who are using shares as collateral may be forced to sell metals. Benchmark December platinum was up 10 yen at 1,342 yen. Benchmark palladium was up one at 448 yen. Benchmark silver December was 1.7 yen per 10 gram up at 178.6 yen.
